transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-10
Start time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Leah Gomez (Redwood SE), Oliver Chen (Redwood CSM); Dana Miller (HavenHealth Dir Eng), Priya Singh (HavenHealth Head of Security), Ethan Cole (HavenHealth ML Infra)

[00:00] Samir Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. we wanted to use this call to nail down success criteria for the pilot and make sure security gates are clear. dana, priya, ethan, do we have the right folks?
[00:12] Dana Miller: yep, that's us. thanks, samir. i pulled priya and ethan in because security and infra are the main blockers.
[00:25] Priya Singh: hi all, quick note, this is an initial security pilot, so our infosec will need SOC 2 and ISO artifacts, plus a answers to a short questionnaire. also SSO via SAML and RBAC are must-haves for the pilot.
[00:40] Leah Gomez: understood. we can share our SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate. on SSO we support SAML and OIDC, and RBAC can be configured per-route. small caveat: some product names in our docs are redwood-infr or similar, transcription often munges that.
[00:58] Ethan Cole: ok, timeline wise, we're hoping to start a two to four week pilot in jan, but we'd like to sign off on security gating before any data moves. also, are audit logs available for all API calls? we need retention for 90 days minimum.
[01:15] Samir Patel: yes, we provide detailed audit logs, with token-level latency/cost breakdowns. retention is configurable; for pilot we typically provide 90 days but we can discuss longer retention as an add-on.
[01:30] Priya Singh: encryption at rest and KMS integrations? we use a managed KMS, prefer customer-managed keys if possible.
[01:40] Leah Gomez: we integrate with customer KMS/HSM via our private deployment or dedicated options. for hosted pilots we have KMS integration options with restricted key use; customer-managed keys are supported for Private deployments.
[01:55] Dana Miller: great. on the success criteria, we have three things: one, meets throughput at 50 qps for short completion prompts; two, latency P95 under 600ms for 256-token requests; three, auditability and RBAC OK with our security team. is that realistic?
[02:15] Leah Gomez: for 50 qps and P95 600ms depends on model choice and quantization. if you use a smaller Llama-family optimized variant on dedicated GPUs we can meet that, for hosted it might be close but depends on concurrency and caching. we'll propose a model/capacity plan in the perf worksheet.
[02:40] Ethan Cole: what about KV cache/prefix caching? our prompts will often have a 100-token patient history prefix. can that be cached to improve latencies?
[02:55] Leah Gomez: yes, continuous prefix/KV caching is part of the runtime; for repeated prefixes we see substantial latency improvements. we'll capture expected hit rates in the benchmark plan.
[03:12] Samir Patel: for the pilot scope i'd recommend starting small: sample of 1000 requests over a day for benching to prove perf, then scale. the bench should include representative prompt lengths and the patient-history prefix.
[03:28] Dana Miller: sounds good. can you share what telemetry we'll get during the pilot? we need request-level traces and token-level cost reports for internal chargebacks.
[03:40] Oliver Chen: yes, the Console exposes per-route token breakdowns, latency histograms, and traces. we can also give you direct csv exports for the pilot.
[03:55] Priya Singh: about SSO: we run Okta; you'll need SAML metadata so our SSO team can test. also, RBAC—can we map groups to roles? we want least privilege.
[04:10] Leah Gomez: we support group-to-role mapping; you can map SAML attributes to roles in the Console. we'll include a SSO setup doc in the artifacts.
[04:25] Ethan Cole: data residency—our PHI workflows require that inference happens in us-east-1 and no logs leave the region for the pilot. is that doable on hosted?
[04:40] Samir Patel: region pinning is supported; hosted can pin to us-east-1 provided capacity. otherwise Dedicated or Private gives stricter guarantees. we will flag potential cross-region backups to legal, but for the pilot we can limit logs to the region, subject to KMS and backup policies. we'll need to document that.
[05:00] Dana Miller: good, also need to confirm whether any raw payload is retained beyond the audit logs and for how long.
[05:12] Leah Gomez: for hosted, by default we retain minimal request metadata; raw input/output retention is opt-in and we can set retention window. Private deployments give you full control. we'll note defaults in the security sheet.
[05:30] Samir Patel: turning to benchmarks: Leah, can you outline the benchmark metrics we'll run?
[05:40] Leah Gomez: sure. we'll run latency (P50/P95/P99), throughput (qps sustained), token cost per request, cache hit rate, and correctness metrics like rouge or a small eval set accuracy depending on your use case. we'll also track resource utilization on GPU.
[06:00] Ethan Cole: for accuracy we use a small labeled set of 200 examples, can that be run as part of the perf test?
[06:10] Leah Gomez: absolutely, include it in the bench harness. we'll provide a runner; you can drop in your labeled set. we'll surface metrics in the report.
[06:25] Priya Singh: will you run any third-party penetration tests during the pilot? our compliance requires at least a vulnerability scan.
[06:35] Samir Patel: we can coordinate. Redwood runs internal scans; we can provide scan reports and can support customer-led pen tests on Dedicated/Private. For hosted pilots, we typically allow a scoped assessment with advance notice. we'll capture the requirements.
[06:55] Dana Miller: okay, timeline — we want security docs before Dec 15 so our procurement and legal can review. pilot kickoff ideally mid-Jan and run 3-4 weeks. is that consistent?
[07:10] Samir Patel: yes, we'll aim to share SOC2/ISO artifacts by Dec 12. pricing and pilot capacity worksheet by Dec 13. then a pre-kickoff checklist call week of Dec 14 to confirm network/VPC needs. mid-Jan start looks good.
[07:30] Ethan Cole: network-wise, if we do hosted with VPC peering, do you support VPC peering, or do we need Private?
[07:45] Leah Gomez: we support VPC peering for Dedicated and Private. Hosted has private networking options via a customer VPC peering add-on in some regions; we'll confirm availability for us-east-1 in the worksheet.
[08:00] Priya Singh: audit logs format — do you ship syslog or do we pull via API? we need logs sent to our SIEM ingest.
[08:12] Oliver Chen: we can stream audit logs to your endpoint or provide API access to pull logs. streaming to an HTTPS collector or S3 export are both options. we'll include details.
[08:30] Dana Miller: what are common failure modes? we want graceful degradation so we don't expose errors to clinicians.
[08:40] Leah Gomez: we provide fallbacks and model variants; you can configure application-facing error policies. for example, if the primary model exceeds latency SLO we can fallback to a simpler model or return a cached response. we'll set those in the rollout policy.
[08:58] Samir Patel: cost: for pilot we often suggest a small Dedicated bucket or hosted with rate caps. we'll send a cost estimate in the worksheet.
[09:10] Ethan Cole: do you do token anonymization or PII masking automatically? privacy is a major concern.
[09:20] Leah Gomez: we provide optional client-side and server-side PII masking tools. masking is configurable; we'll include recommended patterns for PHI.
[09:35] Priya Singh: about RBAC, can we audit role changes? we need an immutable record of role assignments and admin actions.
[09:45] Oliver Chen: yes, role-change events are logged in the audit trail and can be exported.
[10:00] Dana Miller: great. any blockers from your side we should know about?
[10:06] Samir Patel: none on our side; main blockers are your procurement/legal review and network approvals.
[10:15] Leah Gomez: i'll be your technical lead on the bench; i'll create a benchmark plan doc with sample prompts and resource profiles.
[10:30] Ethan Cole: what's included in the security packet? we need contact for escalation and our legal wants the insurance certificate.
[10:40] Samir Patel: we'll include SOC 2 Type II report, ISO 27001 cert, incident response plan summary, contact for escalation, and proof of cyber insurance.
[10:55] Priya Singh: ok thanks. can redwood accommodate a limited data access policy for the pilot so only a few engineers can see outputs?
[11:05] Leah Gomez: yes, role-based access controls allow fine-grained access and we can restrict Console access. we'll propose least-privilege defaults.
[11:22] Dana Miller: let's recap success criteria: throughput 50 qps, P95 < 600ms for 256-token requests, RBAC and audit logs acceptable to infosec, and security artifacts delivered for legal.
[11:35] Samir Patel: correct. action items: we'll share artifacts and the benchmark plan; you provide questionnaire and network topology. then we'll reconvene for pre-kickoff.
[11:50] Priya Singh: timeline notes — questionnaire by Dec 15, bench plan review by Dec 17, pre-kickoff week of Dec 14 then pilot mid-Jan.
[12:05] Oliver Chen: i'll create a shared folder and drop all docs there and send calendar invites for the checklist call.
[12:20] Samir Patel: any other questions?
[12:25] Dana Miller: no further questions, thanks everyone.
[12:30] Samir Patel: great, thanks all. we'll follow up with the security packet and worksheet. bye.

End of meeting.

Notes on transcription quality: some product names may be slightly off (redwood-infer, redwood-infra), speaker labels may be generic when callers dialed via conference. Stutters and overlaps occasionally.
end_of_transcript_notes: Recap and agreed next steps captured in action_items and next_steps fields. Customer requires SOC2/ISO artifacts and SAML SSO; pilot timeline mid-Jan for 3-4 weeks.
